samples.summary: The entire new design-editor suite (~900 lines of tests) is never executed by CI, so none of it can fail
samples.evidence: ci.yml runs vitest only via explicit filters: `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/sheets exec vitest run` (l.57), cli (l.60), docs (l.63), backend (l.66). `grep -r design-editor .github/` returns NO matches at all. packages/design-editor/package.json defines `test: vitest --run` and `typecheck: tsc --noEmit`, but no workflow invokes either. So inject.test.mjs (684 lines), inject.types.test.mts (88 lines), name-keyed-maps.test.mjs (122 lines) and the new jsx-nodes role tests are dead coverage in the pipeline — a regression in inject.mjs would be green. This matters most for inject.types.test.mts, whose only real assertions are type-level and therefore depend entirely on a `tsc` run that does not happen.

samples.summary: The two `@ts-expect-error` tests assert nothing at runtime — `expect(() => f(bad)).not.toThrow()` passes regardless of whether the value is rejected
samples.evidence: `it('rejects a valueKind outside the union')` calls applyLayoutProps('', {…valueKind:'raw'}) and asserts only `.not.toThrow()`. The implementation never throws for any valueKind, and the source is '' so the anchor never resolves — the assertion is true whether or not the union is enforced. Same for `it('rejects an insert missing its index')` (l.72). Their only real check is the `@ts-expect-error` directive, which requires `tsc --noEmit` on this package — and no CI lane runs it (see the CI finding). The test names claim rejection behaviour that nothing verifies.

samples.summary: No end-to-end insert test for the case the jsx-nodes `role: 'container'` change exists to unblock (a conditionally-rendered parent), nor for inserting a sibling after a conditional child — the exact hazard `childSpliceOffset` documents
samples.evidence: jsx-nodes.test.mjs asserts resolveNode now ADMITS `{cond && <div/>}` as a container, but no test in inject.test.mjs ever calls applyLayoutInsert with such a parent and checks the produced text parses. Likewise childSpliceOffset's comment says the offset must come from `prev.owner` because splicing at the element end of `{cond && <div/>}` yields `{cond && <div/> <new/>}` — a syntax error — yet no case in the applyLayoutInsert describe or the involution CASES table has a conditionally-rendered previous sibling. The involution table (SCENE variants, single/nested child, one-line body) contains only plain elements. The regression this reasoning guards against would not be caught.
searchedFor: read 'remove → insert is byte-identical' CASES table

samples.summary: Several distinct rewriteClassLiteral behaviours the code comments call out are untested: repeated-occurrence removal, unsafe `from` in replacements, and partial application (located:true while some tokens were rejected/missing)
samples.evidence: inject.mjs's removals loop deliberately loops `while (next !== null)` to strip every occurrence of a duplicated token; no test in inject.test.mjs supplies a className with the same token twice. The comment on the replacements loop says `from` is checked because 'a `from` carrying whitespace builds a matcher that spans two tokens and deletes a neighbour' — every hostile-token test only exercises `additions`; none passes an unsafe `from`/`to`. And the `rejected` vs `missing` separation is only observed in cases where nothing applies (located:false); there is no test where one valid and one unsafe token are supplied together, which is the case that must return located:true with a rejected note and must not write the unsafe token.

samples.summary: The 'result still parses' assertions use `parseDiagnostics ?? []`, which silently passes if the property is absent
samples.evidence: Every structural safety check is `expect(parse(r.text, 'x.tsx').parseDiagnostics ?? []).toHaveLength(0)`. `parseDiagnostics` is an internal TS SourceFile property; the `?? []` fallback means that if it is ever undefined (different TS version, different construction path) every one of these assertions passes vacuously, including the positive control in 'the refusal stops EXECUTABLE code' — which also uses `?? []` and therefore cannot establish that the mechanism works. A non-optional read, or one assertion that a KNOWN-broken source produces a non-empty diagnostics array, would make these load-bearing.

samples.summary: 'covers every map this package hands out' asserts a hardcoded `toHaveLength(3)`, which cannot detect a new name-keyed export being added without a row
samples.evidence: The test's stated job is to catch an export that lands without a table row, but the only assertion is `expect(NAME_KEYED).toHaveLength(3)` plus a non-empty check per row. Adding a fourth name-keyed export to extract.mjs/jsx-nodes.mjs leaves this test green; it only fails if someone edits the table itself. The enforcement it advertises is delegated back to reviewer discipline — the exact thing the file's header says a table is supposed to replace.

samples.summary: removeImport documents a `default` option in its JSDoc but neither implements nor tests it
samples.evidence: The `@param {{module: string, named?: string[], default?: string}} spec` on removeImport advertises a default binding, but the body only inspects `namedBindings` and returns 'nothing removable' when `!wanted.size`. The removeImport describe has four tests, none passing `default`, so the silent no-op for a documented option ships uncovered.

samples.summary: A set of refusal branches in applyLayoutProps/applyLayoutRemove have no test at all
samples.evidence: Untested reason strings: 'X is already absent' (set.value===null on a missing attribute), 'cannot add X to a fragment', 'node has no direct text child', 'node has multiple text runs', 'could not render a className attribute', the invalid-attribute-name rejection in renderAttribute (only the expression guard is tested), 'cannot remove a root node' (the /whole return value/ test is caught earlier by resolveNode, not by this branch), and 'parent node vanished'. Each is a user-visible answer the client will branch on.
searchedFor: grep 'already absent|multiple text runs|fragment' in test/server/inject.test.mjs

samples.summary: unifiedDiff's LCS_CELL_LIMIT degradation path and its `context` parameter are effectively untested
samples.evidence: The `midA.length * midB.length > LCS_CELL_LIMIT` fallback (a coarse all-minus/all-plus hunk) has no test; the three unifiedDiff tests all use tiny inputs that take the LCS path. `context` is only exercised in inject.types.test.mts:84, whose sole assertion is `expect(typeof s).toBe('string')` — true for any output, so passing 1 vs the default 2 is never observed.

samples.summary:
CRLF handling (`const nl = fileText.includes('
') ? '
' : '
'`) is never exercised in applyLayoutInsert or insertImport
samples.evidence: Both functions branch on CRLF to pick the newline they splice, and applyLayoutInsert additionally splits on /\r?\n/ when re-indenting a snippet. Every fixture in inject.test.mjs uses LF only, so the CRLF branch — which decides whether an edit corrupts line endings in a consumer's file — is uncovered.

samples.summary: The `relocated` reason path is not covered at the inject level for any of the three ops
samples.evidence: applyLayoutProps, applyLayoutInsert and applyLayoutRemove each build a `relocated to path …` reason when resolveNode relocated the anchor by fingerprint — the headline 'path is a HINT, fp is the TRUTH' behaviour. Every anchor in inject.test.mjs is produced by `anchorFor` against the same source, so `r.relocated` is always false and no test ever asserts the relocated reason or that an edit lands on the fingerprinted node after the path went stale.

samples.summary: Envelope/shape tests assert `expect(r.located).toBe(false)` against an empty source, which is trivially true
samples.evidence: `applyLayoutProps('', …)`, `applyLayoutRemove('', …)` and `applyLayoutInsert('', …)` can never locate anything in an empty file, so `toBe(false)` holds independently of the behaviour under test. The type annotations on the left-hand side are the real assertion, which again depends on a tsc run this package does not get in CI.

samples.summary: The 'positive control' partly re-asserts a string the test itself built
samples.evidence: `expect(injected).toContain('onMouseOver={fetch(`//evil`)}')` where `injected` is a template literal the test just concatenated from EVIL — true by construction, not by any behaviour of inject.mjs. Only the parseDiagnostics half of that test says anything about the parser (and see the `?? []` finding).

finding.summary: The entire new design-editor suite (~900 lines of tests) is never executed by CI, so none of it can fail
finding.evidence: ci.yml runs vitest only via explicit filters: `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/sheets exec vitest run` (l.57), cli (l.60), docs (l.63), backend (l.66). `grep -r design-editor .github/` returns NO matches at all. packages/design-editor/package.json defines `test: vitest --run` and `typecheck: tsc --noEmit`, but no workflow invokes either. So inject.test.mjs (684 lines), inject.types.test.mts (88 lines), name-keyed-maps.test.mjs (122 lines) and the new jsx-nodes role tests are dead coverage in the pipeline — a regression in inject.mjs would be green. This matters most for inject.types.test.mts, whose only real assertions are type-level and therefore depend entirely on a `tsc` run that does not happen.

verdict.reason: The design-editor suite IS executed by CI, via an indirect chain the reviewer's greps did not follow. ci.yml:54 runs `pnpm verify:self` (a plain step with no continue-on-error, unlike the backend coverage step at l.67) -> root package.json:21 maps that to scripts/verify-self.mjs -> verify-self.mjs:98 declares the lane { name: "verify:fast", cmd: "pnpm verify:fast" } -> root package.json:12 ends verify:fast with `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/design-editor typecheck && pnpm --filter @wafflebase/design-editor test`, i.e. exactly the two scripts claimed to be un-invoked. Failures propagate: verify-self.mjs:356-367 sets failed=true on a nonzero lane exit and :385-387 calls process.exit(1), so a regression in inject.mjs fails the lane and the job rather than being green. The lane's only skip path (:290-302) fires solely when an earlier lane already failed (fail-fast), at which point CI is already red. The finding's strongest sub-claim -- that inject.types.test.mts depends on a tsc run that never happens -- is also false: packages/design-editor/tsconfig.json:52 sets include ["src","test"], and the type tests live under test/server/, so `tsc --noEmit` covers them. The reviewer's literal observation that grep design-editor .github/ returns nothing is true but not load-bearing, because this repo dispatches tests through a runner script rather than naming packages in YAML. The only genuine residue is that design-editor lcov is absent from the Codecov upload list (ci.yml:72-77) -- a coverage-reporting gap, not dead tests, and not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: The two `@ts-expect-error` tests assert nothing at runtime — `expect(() => f(bad)).not.toThrow()` passes regardless of whether the value is rejected
finding.evidence: `it('rejects a valueKind outside the union')` calls applyLayoutProps('', {…valueKind:'raw'}) and asserts only `.not.toThrow()`. The implementation never throws for any valueKind, and the source is '' so the anchor never resolves — the assertion is true whether or not the union is enforced. Same for `it('rejects an insert missing its index')` (l.72). Their only real check is the `@ts-expect-error` directive, which requires `tsc --noEmit` on this package — and no CI lane runs it (see the CI finding). The test names claim rejection behaviour that nothing verifies.

verdict.reason:
The two tests are type-level tests, and their real assertion (`@ts-expect-error`) IS enforced by a CI lane, contrary to the finding's supporting claim.

What I verified in the repo:
1. The tests exist as described (inject.types.test.mts:55-65 and :72-77) and their runtime assertion is indeed only `.not.toThrow()`. So the literal quote is accurate — but the conclusion drawn from it is not.
2. The file's header (inject.types.test.mts:10-24) states explicitly that its purpose is to be a *TypeScript consumer* of the `// @ts-check`+JSDoc `inject.mjs`, so a JSDoc signature drift fails `pnpm typecheck`. The `.not.toThrow()` is a vehicle to place the call expression, not the claimed coverage.
3. The constraints the directives assert are real, non-trivial JSDoc types: `valueKind?: 'string'|'expression'` (src/server/inject.mjs:415, consumed at :508 and the `'string'|'expression'` param at :390) and `index: number` required in the insert intent (src/server/inject.mjs:591). So `@ts-expect-error` genuinely fires; if the union were widened or `index` made optional, tsc would report "Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive" and fail — the directive is bidirectional, i.e. a real assertion that fails when the behavior changes.
4. The claim "no CI lane runs `tsc --noEmit` on this package" is false. packages/design-editor/package.json:8 defines `typecheck: tsc --noEmit`; packages/design-editor/tsconfig.json:52 includes `"test"`, so these `.mts` files are in the program; root package.json:12 (`verify:fast`) ends with `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/design-editor typecheck && ... test`; scripts/verify-self.mjs:98 runs `verify:fast` as a lane; and .github/workflows/ci.yml:54 runs `pnpm verify:self` on every push/PR to main.

So there is no fake coverage here: the rejection behavior the test names claim is verified at compile time by a check that runs in the merge-gating CI lane. Not a blocking test-adequacy defect.

verdict.reason: The absence is real. `childSpliceOffset` (inject.mjs:308-344) takes the insert/remove offset from `prev.owner.getEnd()` specifically because splicing at the element end inside `{cond && <div/>}` yields a syntax error, and `childrenOf` (jsx-nodes.mjs:298-327) numbers conditional children, so a conditionally-rendered `prev` is genuinely reachable through `applyLayoutInsert` (inject.mjs:624). Repo-wide, `applyLayoutInsert` is only called from inject.test.mjs and the type-only inject.types.test.mts (which passes `''` and never exercises offsets). In inject.test.mjs the applyLayoutInsert describe (202-268) and the involution CASES table (277-284) use only plain-element sources; the sole conditional source (356-361) is an applyLayoutRemove refusal at index 0, where `prev` is null and the owner branch is never taken. The nearest coverage — jsx-nodes.test.mjs:203-207 (`owner !== node`) and 307-313 (`role:'container'` admits a conditional element) — asserts on jsx-nodes internals only; neither performs an insert nor parses the result, so a regression changing `prev.owner.getEnd()` to `prev.node.getEnd()` would emit unparseable JSX with no failing test. Major under the missing-tests rubric: a documented, reachable hazard in changed code with no meaningful test.

verdict.reason: All three claimed gaps hold up against the repository. inject.mjs:213-226 loops `while (next !== null)` to strip repeated occurrences, but every removals test uses `['wrap']` against `className="wrapper wrap gap-2"` (one token match) or `['nope']` (inject.test.mjs:119, 171, 181) — no className supplies the same token twice, so the loop body never runs a second time. inject.mjs:197-201 checks `safe(from)` specifically because a whitespace-bearing `from` builds a matcher spanning two tokens; the only `replacements` test (inject.test.mjs:485) passes `{from:'text-sm', to:'$&-$&'}`, both safe, so that branch is never taken. And the partial-application path (inject.mjs:438-444: `rejected` note emitted while `n > 0` still splices, returning located:true) is never exercised: every hostile test (inject.test.mjs:395-448) passes a single-element `additions` array and asserts `located===false` / `text===src`; no test mixes one valid and one unsafe token. I confirmed no other test reaches this code: `rewriteClassLiteral` has a single caller (`applyLayoutProps`), and a repo-wide grep for `applyLayoutProps|isSafeClassToken|removeClassToken` finds only inject.test.mjs and inject.types.test.mts, the latter being a type-only consumer whose calls all pass `''` and assert located===false. name-keyed-maps.test.mjs contains no classOps/applyLayoutProps reference at all. In-lane for test adequacy: distinct, deliberately-commented behaviours of a module that writes to a user's working tree, shipped with no covering assertions.
